blocks.text: You can limit the properties a component receives by using destructuring.

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
React uses curly brackets to destructure props:
  {color}.
You can also destruct the properties you need inside the component.
This way, the component receives all the properties, but the destructuring makes sure it only uses the ones it needs.

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: When you don't know how many properties you will receive, you can use the ...rest operator.
Meaning: you can specify the properties you need, and the rest will be stored in an object.

blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: With Destructuring, you can set default values for props.
If a property has no value, the default value will be used.
